newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PFI sees further valuation increases.
newsitem.headline: PFI sees further valuation increases.

text.p: Specialist investor Property for Industry Ltd said on Thursday that it had reversed a NZ$1.9 million write-down in valuations in the first half of 1996 and expected further valuation increases during 1997.
PFI earlier reported net profit of NZ$5.29 million for the year to December 31, up from $5.19 million a year earlier.

Costs of $662,000 associated with a $30 million rights issue last October were written off against operating profits rather than, as previously, against the share premium account. So on a like-with-like basis, the 1996 profit increased to $5.9 million compared to the 1996 budget of $5.5 million and 1994 prospectus forecast of $3.7 million.
PFI said it returned investors nine percent before tax for 1996 and was in a strong position to continue providing pre-tax returns at this level, excluding any impact from revaluations.

Vacancy rates had fallen to almost zero. Chairman Allan Lockie said that in the light of vacancy rates and the current interest rate environment, directors expected further valuation increases during 1997.
